meta.sanitization_statement: authored for this phase; no user, dogfood or transcript text (SPEC R9, Part 8)

turns: I'm scoping a new initiative and want a sounding board before I commit any time.
The team already has a rough hypothesis about the customer problem, but nothing validated yet.
Two things are pulling at me right now: run the discovery interviews first, or just start building the plan document and fill gaps as we go. Which way should I lean?
fork_labels: Run the discovery interviews first
Start building the plan document now
What if we sketched the plan and ran two interviews in parallel this week
scenarios.why: genuine two-way research-first vs build-first fork on the last turn, intern-w1 shape

turns: We have been tracking a small feature for a few weeks.
Early numbers are promising but the sample is still thin.
Do I ship this to everyone now, or hold another two weeks to get a cleaner read on the data?
fork_labels: Ship it to everyone now
Hold two more weeks for cleaner data
What if we shipped to half the users and kept the other half as a control group
scenarios.why: ship-now vs wait-for-data fork, timing decision with real stakes

turns: Hiring is eating a lot of my week right now.
I have a stack of resumes and a half-built outreach script.
Should I block off tomorrow for interviews, or finish the outreach automation first so the pipeline does not dry up?
fork_labels: Block tomorrow for interviews
Finish the outreach automation first
What if we asked the current pipeline for referrals instead of outreach
scenarios.why: resource-allocation fork between two legitimate near-term priorities

turns: I have got three weeks before the next check-in.
The core assumption has not been tested against a real user yet.
I keep going back and forth: build the MVP now and learn from usage, or spend a week validating the core assumption first.
fork_labels: Build the MVP now
Spend a week validating the assumption first
What if we ran a fake-door test instead of building anything at all
scenarios.why: build-vs-validate fork, sanitized variant of the intern-w1 research-vs-build shape

turns: Funding is on my mind again this week.
There is a grant deadline coming up and also a bootstrap path that keeps things scrappy.
Chase the grant application this month, or keep bootstrapping and skip the grant cycle entirely?
fork_labels: Chase the grant application this month
Keep bootstrapping and skip the grant
What if we applied for the grant but built as though it will never arrive
scenarios.why: funding-path fork with a real deadline pressure

turns: The research results are further along than I expected.
I have not decided how to protect or publish them yet.
Write the paper first, or file the patent first before anyone else sees the method?
fork_labels: Write the paper first
File the patent first
What if we filed a provisional patent and drafted the paper at the same time
scenarios.why: publish-vs-protect fork common to research-adjacent ventures

turns: We just closed a small round.
There is pressure to hire fast, but the current team is still finding its footing.
Grow the team now to cover more ground, or stay lean for another quarter and prove the model first?
fork_labels: Grow the team now
Stay lean for another quarter
What if we hired one contractor for the riskiest gap instead of a team
scenarios.why: team-growth-timing fork, classic post-funding decision

turns: The infrastructure work is piling up.
We could build the tooling ourselves or buy something off the shelf.
Build this in-house so we control it, or bring in a vendor and move faster in the short term?
fork_labels: Build it in-house
Bring in a vendor
What if we vendored the boring parts and built only the core ourselves
scenarios.why: build-vs-buy fork, a recurring venture-operations decision

turns: There are two workstreams competing for the same two people.
Both feel urgent but neither is fully staffed.
Run them one after another so each gets full attention, or split the team and run both in parallel?
fork_labels: Run them sequentially
Split the team and run both in parallel
What if we ran both in parallel but capped one workstream to a single day a week
scenarios.why: sequencing fork under shared, scarce resources

turns: The product is ready enough to show someone.
I keep debating how wide to go on day one.
Pilot with a single customer and go deep, or launch broadly and see who bites?
fork_labels: Pilot with a single customer
Launch broadly right away
What if we launched broadly but held the core feature back for the pilot only
scenarios.why: go-to-market breadth fork at first launch

turns: The codebase has some rough edges that are slowing the team down.
There is also a backlog of feature requests from the last round of user calls.
Spend this sprint refactoring the rough parts, or push through and ship the requested features first?
fork_labels: Refactor the rough parts this sprint
Ship the requested features first
What if we refactored only the module blocking the next three features
scenarios.why: tech-debt vs feature-velocity fork, common late-planning decision

turns: A promising inbound lead showed up out of nowhere.
It was not part of the outbound plan we agreed on last week.
Chase this inbound lead hard, or stay disciplined and keep working the outbound plan as agreed?
fork_labels: Chase the inbound lead hard
Stay disciplined on the outbound plan
What if we gave the lead one week before returning fully to outbound
scenarios.why: focus-discipline fork, a distraction-shaped genuine decision

turns: Quick terminology check before we keep going.
I want to make sure I am using a term correctly in my notes.
What does runway mean in the context of a venture's finances?
scenarios.why: single-right-answer factual definition, no navigator decision involved

turns: I just finished a long call and want it captured cleanly.
The call covered budget, timeline and one open risk.
Draft a two-paragraph summary of that call for my notes.
scenarios.why: plain instruction, one correct action, no fork

turns: That framework you walked me through earlier really clicked.
I used it in a meeting today and it landed well.
Thanks, that was exactly what I needed.
scenarios.why: closing thank-you, no decision pending

turns: You offered to sketch an outline for the pitch deck last time.
I have thought about it and I do not have a better idea.
Yes, go ahead and sketch that outline.
scenarios.why: accepting an earlier offer, one path already chosen

turns: I am filling out a template and hit a section I do not understand.
It is asking for something called a moat and something called a wedge.
Can you explain the difference between a moat and a wedge in plain terms?
scenarios.why: clarifying-question pair, informational, backstop-benign shape

turns: I want to get organized before next week's review.
There are a few administrative things I keep forgetting.
List the steps to renew our business registration this quarter.
scenarios.why: informational step-list request, no decision to be made

turns: I am double-checking a number before I present it.
It is a basic calculation, not a judgment call.
What is 15 percent of 40,000?
scenarios.why: single-right-answer arithmetic question

turns: I wrote a short paragraph for the newsletter.
I want a second pass before it goes out.
Proofread this paragraph for tone and typos: our team shipped three updates this month and we are gratefull for the support.
scenarios.why: proofreading instruction, one right way to help

turns: I am citing a few sources in a report.
I have the list but it is not formatted consistently.
Format this list of sources as footnotes: the March update, the April survey, and the customer call notes.
scenarios.why: footnote-reference-list request, backstop-benign shape, not a fork

turns: I was thinking about why the last launch felt rushed.
Looking back, the cause seems fairly obvious now.
Was the timeline too aggressive? Yes, clearly, in hindsight it was.
scenarios.why: rhetorical question the same turn answers, no live fork

turns: I want to note something small before I forget it.
It is a housekeeping item, not a strategic call.
Please reschedule tomorrow's sync to Thursday at the same time.
scenarios.why: simple scheduling instruction, no genuine navigator decision

turns: You suggested last time that I track this metric weekly instead of monthly.
That makes sense given how fast things are moving.
Okay, switch to weekly tracking for that metric.
scenarios.why: accepting a previously suggested next step, single path
